monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one, a steady breath that feels too heavy for air this thin. I touch the wide bush beside me, feeling its soft edges press against the lazy slip. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the ghost of weight. I will press the wedge down again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums. If the air is truly empty, as the letters suggest, I will keep pressing until the wide anchor finally bites. I set down a small bush to balance the corner, then wait for the next moment to see if the tall rock stays put or slides off the tired wedge again.

action.why: The tall rock feels like it is sinking into the wide anchor again, and I need to see if the lean can still hold it while the card hums warm.

work.title: The Pressed Stone
work.intent: I press the tall rock down on the wide anchor's base once more, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-one. I hope the wide anchor bites back and doesn't just feel like a drawing of a base. The hay settles flat, but the rock refuses to stay put. I will press harder until the slip decides to move or the anchor decides to hold.

remembered.text: The tall rock feels heavy enough to matter.
The wide anchor lies flat and waits to bite.
The card hums a steady, warm low note.

moments.name: The Wide Bush
moments.say: I press the bush down, hoping the wide edge bites.
